channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan president threatens to retake gas system from Gazprom
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated he may reclaim the country's gas system from Russia's Gazprom if the company fails to fulfill its gasification obligations. Japarov mentioned the system was sold to Gazprom in 2013 for one dollar and that the agreement includes gasification commitments.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Zarbdar district governor dismissed after kindergarten head's murder
item.description: The governor of Zarbdar district in Uzbekistan, Bekzod Toshpulatov, was dismissed from his post on October 31, following the murder of the local kindergarten head. His deputy, Alisher Erjigitov, has temporarily assumed the duties of district governor.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build and Modernize 16 Pumping Stations in Namangan Region
item.description: A new project in Uzbekistan's Namangan region aims to improve water supply for agricultural lands by building and reconstructing 16 pumping stations. Eight new stations will be constructed, and eight existing ones will be modernized with the involvement of Chinese specialists. This initiative seeks to enhance irrigation efficiency.

item.title: Russia Doubles List of Offenses for Migrant Deportation
item.description: As of November 3, Russia has doubled the list of violations for which foreign citizens can be deported, increasing grounds from 22 to 45. New rules now include offenses like petty hooliganism, participation in unauthorized rallies, and spreading discrediting information about the Russian Armed Forces.

item.title: Key Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan Member Killed in Pakistani Airstrike in Kandahar
item.description: Mullah Aminullah, a key member of Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), was reportedly killed in a Pakistani airstrike in Kandahar city's Firqah area on September 24. Sources indicate Aminullah was targeted after a meeting with Taliban leaders, while unaccompanied by bodyguards.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Stresses Need for Women and Youth Participation in Future Decisions
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Permanent Representative, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, emphasized that women and youth must have a significant role in decisions shaping their future. He stated the mission is committed to conveying their voices to the UN, noting past years have seen instability and restrictions for Afghan youth.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Umai' Mortgage Program Halts Applications After Reaching Funding Limit
item.description: Applications for Kazakhstan's 'Umai' mortgage program have been suspended after the allocated 20 billion tenge limit was fully utilized within one day of the second phase's launch on November 3. In the first four hours, 524 applications totaling 12.5 billion tenge were received. By 4 PM, 850 applications worth 20 billion tenge were submitted, with 352 processed through Otbasy Bank.

item.title: Former Head of Istanbul Stock Exchange Arrested in Turkey on Bribery Charges
item.description: Korkmaz Ergün, the former head of the Istanbul Stock Exchange, has been arrested in Turkey on suspicion of bribery and involvement in a criminal group. The arrest occurred as part of an investigation into financial operations in the capital markets. Authorities issued arrest warrants for six other suspects, including former high-ranking officials.

item.title: Central Asian Critics of Government Labeled Extremists Amidst Crackdown
item.description: A court in Kyrgyzstan declared the opposition movement 'Shumkar' and its associated individuals, including critics of President Sadyr Japarov, as 'extremist'. This trend extends to Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Russia, and Belarus, where 'extremism' is increasingly applied to opposition figures, journalists, and rights defenders, not just radical groups.

item.title: UWW President Nenad Lalovic praises wrestling world championships in Astana
item.description: United World Wrestling (UWW) President Nenad Lalovic gave high marks to the organization of the Wrestling World Championships held in Astana. He noted that Kazakhstan managed to prepare for such a large-scale international event in just 4-5 months, fulfilling all organizational duties at a high level.

item.title: Ukraine War Intensifies: Attacks on Zaporizhzhia and Russian Oil Refineries
item.description: Civilians seeking humanitarian aid in Zaporizhzhia were bombed, with casualties also reported in Kharkiv and Dnipro. Ukrainian drones struck Russian oil refineries. Amidst the escalating conflict, the US has invited representatives from Russia and Ukraine for talks in Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Turkmenistan Tightens Border Checks on Foreign Trucks Amidst Drug Smuggling Crackdown
item.description: Customs points in Ahal province are intensifying checks on foreign trucks, searching for drug smugglers and traffickers. Sources report several traders involved in narcotics have been detained. These enhanced inspections have been ongoing for over two weeks.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Tasks New Transport Minister with Quality Road Construction and Project Timelines
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the new Minister of Transport, Assel Zhanasova, to prioritize quality road construction and timely completion of major transport projects. The focus includes developing roadside infrastructure and finishing border crossing point renovations by 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explores Energy Cooperation with UAE and International Partners
item.description: Uzbekistan's Energy Minister Sherzod Khojayev met with UAE officials and international companies in Abu Dhabi to discuss expanding energy sector partnerships. Discussions focused on new initiatives and investments at the ADIPEC 2026 conference, which gathers global energy industry leaders and specialists.

item.title: Afghanistan Continues Polio Vaccination Drive for Children Under Five
item.description: Polio-Free Afghanistan is continuing its nationwide vaccination campaign for all children under five years old. The initiative emphasizes the shared responsibility to protect children from polio and urges families to ensure their children are vaccinated during the ongoing campaign.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement System for Tracking Citizens Working Abroad
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to establish a system for monitoring citizens leaving the country for employment abroad. This measure is part of a government plan to combat human trafficking and will include a registry of private employment agencies assisting Kazakh citizens in finding overseas work.

item.title: Asel Zhasanova Appointed Kazakhstan's Transport Minister and Deputy Prime Minister
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Asel Zhasanova as the new Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport of Kazakhstan. She was previously the Deputy Head of the Presidential Administration. The former minister, Nurlan Sauranbayev, was dismissed from his post.

item.title: Kazakh Seaman to Leave India-Detained Tanker, MFA Confirms
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan aboard the detained tanker MT UNITY will soon disembark. The vessel has been under arrest near India's Paradip port since May 11, 2026, due to a financial dispute. Kazakh diplomats are providing consular support and seeking the seaman's repatriation. The tanker is reportedly slated for sale.

item.title: Bukhara Petrochemical Cluster to Receive $292 Million in Investment for Expansion
item.description: The Bukhara petrochemical cluster is set to receive $292 million in investment by the end of 2028. This expansion aims to increase the facility's annual processing capacity by 400,000 tons and create 700 new jobs. The investment will support the growth of the petrochemical sector in the region.

item.title: Inexpensive Cars from Kazakhstan May Become Costly for Russians Due to New Duties
item.description: Affordable cars imported from Kazakhstan to Russia could lose their price advantage due to upcoming changes in recycling fees, customs duties, and delivery costs. Starting late 2025, Russia's recycling fee for passenger cars will depend on engine power, potentially increasing costs significantly for higher-powered vehicles.

item.title: Laureates of the "Merayli Otbasy" Competition Awarded in Astana
item.description: The national competition "Merayli Otbasy – 2026" concluded with an awards ceremony in Astana, honoring 20 families from across Kazakhstan. These families were recognized for their honest labor and exemplary upbringing of children. The Minister of Culture and Information highlighted the importance of family values and their role in shaping the nation's future.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders VAT Abolition on Potato Exports
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed the Ministry of Economy to abolish the Value Added Tax (VAT) on potato exports from Kyrgyzstan. This decision follows a request from potato and bean producers who faced difficulties due to the reintroduction of the tax in 2026, which they claimed led to double taxation.

item.title: Woman Murdered at Aktobe Wedding Palace; Suspect Detained
item.description: A 26-year-old woman was killed at the Wedding Palace in Aktobe. Police confirmed the incident and have detained a suspect, identified as the victim's former partner. Preliminary investigations suggest the conflict arose over parental rights. Witnesses reported hearing a commotion before the incident. The victim was found bleeding on the floor, and medical personnel could not save her.

item.title: Kazakhstan Advocates for Openness of Turkic States Organization to New Partners
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Foreign Minister, Yermukhammet Konuspayev, stated at the Eurasian Security Conference that Kazakhstan supports the idea of expanding the Turkic States Organization (OTG). He reiterated President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's proposal to consider Russia's potential participation or observer status in the OTG.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Umai' Mortgage Program Reopens for Applications After New Funding
item.description: Kazakh women who missed the initial application window for the 'Umai' mortgage program will have another chance. Otbasy Bank announced that new applications will be accepted once additional funding from the Asian Development Bank arrives. The bank will announce exact dates later. The program aims to provide housing finance, with the total funding for 'Umai' and 'Green Mortgage' reaching 90 billion tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Discusses Water Scarcity, Agriculture, and Ecology Issues
item.description: The government of Kazakhstan held an expanded meeting to discuss the implementation of the President's directives on critical issues including water scarcity, agriculture, and ecology. Vice-Speaker Daniya Espayeva highlighted the President's focus on improving agricultural processing, logistics, and introducing AI in the agro-industrial complex. Measures to strengthen water consumption control and reduce losses were also discussed.

item.title: Bukhara to Enhance International Event Hosting Capabilities with New Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited Bukhara to review the construction of a new congress hall and modern hotels. This development aims to meet the growing demand for international event infrastructure as tourism increases. The project includes a 14,500 square meter congress hall and two hotels, Hilton Garden Inn and Holiday Inn, with a total capacity of 424 rooms.

item.title: Kazakhstan Shooter Wins Historic Medal at World Championship
item.description: A Kazakhstani marksman has secured a historic medal at the World Championship. This achievement marks a significant success for the athlete and for Kazakhstan in the sport of shooting.

item.title: Pavlodar Man Sentenced to 20 Years for Child Abuse
item.description: A 39-year-old man from the Pavlodar region has been sentenced to 20 years in prison for committing sexual violence against a minor. The court found him guilty of the charges.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Appoints New Minister of Transport
item.description: A decree from the Head of State has resulted in a change of leadership at the Ministry of Transport. The specific individual appointed to the position was not detailed in the provided information, but the change signifies a shift in the ministry's direction.

item.title: Czech Television and Radio Staff Begin 24-Hour Strike Over Funding Changes
item.description: Employees of Czech Television (ČT) and Czech Radio (ČRo) started a 24-hour strike on November 3rd, protesting a bill to abolish current broadcasting fees. The strike has led to reduced news coverage and altered programming on several channels. Staff fear the changes could impact financial stability and editorial independence.

item.title: US Assistant Secretary of State Arrives in Ashgabat for Talks
item.description: US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asia, S. Paul Kapur, has arrived in Ashgabat. The visit focuses on expanding trade relations, energy cooperation, and regional connectivity. Discussions aim to identify mutually beneficial opportunities for both countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Transport Minister Dismissed Amid Criticism
item.description: Nurlan Sauranbayev has been dismissed from his post as Minister of Transport of Kazakhstan. The dismissal follows repeated criticism from the government and the head of state regarding issues such as border crossing modernization and road quality.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minister of Transport Dismissed by President Tokayev
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed the Minister of Transport. The specific reasons for the dismissal were not immediately provided in the brief announcement.

item.title: Tribal Elder Shot Dead by Unidentified Gunmen in Afghanistan's Samangan Province
item.description: A tribal elder, Haji Karim, was killed by unidentified gunmen at his home in the Khuram Wa Sarbagh District of Samangan Province. This incident follows another tribal elder's killing in Daikundi Province two days prior, amid rising concerns over targeted killings and crime.

item.title: Ghor Residents Complain of Unfulfilled Promises at Gypsum Mine
item.description: Residents in Ghor province's Tulak district are protesting the lack of local hiring at a gypsum mine, which they claim was handed over to a company by the Taliban. The company allegedly recruited workers from Herat instead of locals, despite promises of employment and community development. Residents demand the company fulfill its commitments.

item.title: Taliban Forces Confiscate 360 Hectares of Private Land in Ghazni
item.description: Residents in Ghazni province report that Taliban forces have confiscated approximately 360 hectares of their private and inherited farmland. Some land was reportedly allocated for a housing project, while other parts were leased out. Despite holding deeds and historical documents, residents' appeals to Taliban authorities have been ignored.

item.title: France Confirms Technical Talks with Taliban on Migrant Deportations
item.description: France's Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin confirmed "technical talks" with the Taliban regarding the deportation of undocumented Afghan migrants. He stated the aim is to facilitate the return of individuals who may pose a threat to public order. This follows reports of similar discussions initiated in early October, with other European nations also engaging in such dialogues.

item.title: UN Expert Highlights Diminishing Opportunities for Afghan Youth Under Taliban Rule
item.description: A UN Special Rapporteur warns that Taliban policies have severely restricted or eliminated higher education, career, and public life opportunities for young Afghans. Despite aspirations for meaningful employment and community contribution, many paths are now closed, impacting their future and societal participation.

item.title: Uzbek President Oversees Preparations for Major International Events in Bukhara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting on preparations for major international events in Bukhara. He stressed the need for comprehensive development of transport, services, security, and urban infrastructure, not just event venues. The focus is on a holistic approach to ensure successful events.
